  Regular Meeting Agenda
  CITY COUNCIL

Tuesday, July 9, 2024  7:00 PM  Council Chamber

NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's web site under City Council Meeting agendas at www.RollingHillsEstates.gov and
  during regular business hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's web
  site and a recording is available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP -TV
  Channel 35 (Cox) and Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome on any item during City Council consideration of the item. An opportunity is
  also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If you would like to
  address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public comment, please
  complete a speaker sheet and give to the City Clerk.

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

3.  ROLL CALL

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

  NONE

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR
  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the
  City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member
  prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on separately.)

  A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS
  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to the
  City Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read by
  title only.

  Recommendation: Receive and file.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS
  This is the appropriate time for members of the public to make comments regarding items not listed on this
  agenda. If you would like to address the City Council, please complete a speaker sheet and give to the
  City Clerk. Under the State's open meeting law - the Brown Act - no action may be taken on any item not
  on the agenda.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 230037
  COMPREHENSIVE ZONING CODE UPDATE
  LOCATION: CITYWIDE
  Memorandum from Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1. Take public testimony; 2. Discuss
  Ordinance No. 749; 3. Close the public hearing; 4. Conduct the second reading and
  adopt Ordinance No. 749.
  Attachments: Staff Report + Ordinance No. 749

8.  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  AWARD OF PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACT TO BONADIMAN WATER INC.
  (BWI) TO MAKE STORM DRAIN REPAIRS/REPLACEMENT ON PALOS
  VERDES DRIVE EAST (PVDE) AND TO CONSTRUCT A DRY WELL
  STORM DRAIN INFILTRATION SYSTEM ON PVDE & BRIDLEWOOD
  CIRCLE
  Memorandum from David Wahba, Director of Public Works
  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1. Award a Public Works Contract to
  Bonadiman Water Inc. (BWI) to make storm drain repairs/replacements on Palos
  Verdes Drive East (PVDE) and to construct a dry well storm drain infiltration system,
  in the amount of $1,637,750, plus a 10% contingency ($163,775) for a total of
  $1,801,525; and, 2. Authorize $15,000 for Public Works Permits and inspections to
  be provided by Willdan Engineering.
  Attachments: Staff Report

  B.  MASTER PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT (MPSA) WITH RISK
  MANAGEMENT  PROFESSIONALS  INCORPORATED  FOR  THE
  DEVELOPMENT OF AN EMERGENCY OPERATIONS PLAN
  Memorandum from Jessica Slawson, Assistant to the City Manager
  Recommendation: That the City Council Approve a 1) Master Professional Services
  Agreement (MPSA) approved as to form by the City Attorney with Risk
  Management Professionals Incorporated, and 2) Task Order 1-2024, under the
  MPSA in the not-to-exceed amount of $25,000.
  Attachments: Staff Report

  C.  LETTER OF OPPOSITION TO AB 3093 (WARD) LAND USE: HOUSING
  ELEMENT: STREAMLINED MULTIFAMILY HOUSING
  Memorandum from Greg Grammer, City Manager and Jessica Slawson, Assistant to
  the City Manager
  Recommendation: That the City Council approve and authorize the Mayor to sign the
  letter of opposition.
  Attachments: Staff Report

 City Council  Regular Meeting Agenda  July 9, 2024

  D.  MASTER PROFESSIONAL  SERVICES  AGREEMENT  AND  ANNUAL
  AUDIT ENGAGEMENT LETTER TASK ORDER
  Memorandum from Fernando Estrada, Senior Accountant and Michael Whitehead,
  Administrative Services Director
  Recommendation: That the City of Rolling Hills Estates approve the master
  professional services agreement as approved to form by the City Attorney and Task
  Order No. 2024-01 for the firm of Rogers, Anderson, Malody & Scott, LLP to
  perform the annual audit and report for Fiscal Year 2023-24; perform the single
  audit, if needed; prepare the Pepper Tree Foundation’s tax returns; and review the
  GANN appropriation limitation for a total amount not to exceed $51,405.
  Attachments: Staff Report

9.  OLD BUSINESS

  A.  QUARTERLY  2023-2024 WORK  PLAN  UPDATE  AND  WORK  PLAN
  2024-2025
  Memorandum from Greg Grammer, City Manager
  Recommendation: Receive and file.
  Attachments: Staff Report

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

11.  CITY COUNCIL / REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS
  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and reports to
  other Members of the City Council and the public on any issues or activities of Council Committees, ad
  hoc committees, regional or state-wide governmental associations, special districts, joint powers
  authorities and the various committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or have an
  interest, which are not otherwise agendized.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS
  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to request information on currently
  pending projects and/or issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future consideration
  and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

13.  CLOSED SESSION
  If you would like to address the City Council regarding an item on the Closed Session agenda, please

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JULY 9, 2024

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

City Clerk Pettit called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  Schmitz, Stegura

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Attorney Stephen McEwen
  Public Works Director David Wahba
  Community Development Director Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Assistant to the City Manager Jessica Slawson

In the absence of the Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem and by a majority consensus, the present
Council Members selected COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN to preside over the meeting.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Assistant to the City Manager Jessica Slawson.

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

None.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-E AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Schmitz, Stegura

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF JUNE & JULY 2024

  APPROVED WARRANTS 67504 THROUGH 67543 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $399,111.68, AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 070124 THROUGH
  070324 IN THE AMOUNT OF $129,565.96; FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT
  OF $528,677.64 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  CITY COUNCIL ADJOURNED MINUTES OF JUNE 25, 2024

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

D.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JUNE 25, 2024

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
JULY 9, 2024
 E.  SOUTH BAY CITIES COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS BOARD MEETING
  HIGHLIGHTS OF

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT/PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

E-Comment received from Brandee Keith of South Coast Air Quality Management District
(AQMD) announcing the 10th Annual Environmental Justice Conference on October 24, 2024.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 230037
  COMPREHENSIVE ZONING CODE UPDATE
  LOCATION: CITYWIDE

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1. Take public testimony; 2. Discuss
  Ordinance No. 749; 3. Close the public hearing; 4. Conduct the second reading and
  adopt Ordinance No. 749.

Community Development Director Naughton provided a summary of the staff report (as per
the staff report).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Schmitz, Stegura

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  CONDUCT A SECOND READING AND ADOPT ORDINANCE NO. 749, AN
  ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES, CALIFORNIA, ADOPTING VARIOUS AMENDMENTS TO THE
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO TITLE 17
  (ZONING) AND REZONING CERTAIN PROPERTIES TO CONFORM WITH
  THE CITY’S 2040 GENERAL PLAN, AND DETERMINING THE CODE
  AMENDMENTS AND PROPERTY REZONINGS ARE EXEMPT FROM THE
  CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Schmitz, Stegura

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance No. 749 by title.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  AWARD OF PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACT TO BONADIMAN WATER INC. (BWI) TO
  MAKE STORM DRAIN REPAIRS/REPLACEMENT ON PALOS VERDES DRIVE
  EAST (PVDE) AND TO CONSTRUCT A DRY WELL STORM DRAIN INFILTRATION
  SYSTEM ON PVDE & BRIDLEWOOD CIRCLE

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1. Award a Public Works Contract to
  Bonadiman Water Inc. (BWI) to make storm drain repairs/replacements on Palos
  Verdes Drive East (PVDE) and to construct a dry well storm drain infiltration system,
  in the amount of $1,637,750, plus a 10% contingency ($163,775) for a total of

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JULY 9, 2024
   $1,801,525; and, 2. Authorize $15,000 for Public Works Permits and inspections to
  be provided by Willdan Engineering.

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material) and added
that BWI has submitted a request for bid relief due to a clerical error

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN confirmed that staff is working with BWI to determine the
nature of the clerical error.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  DIRECT STAFF TO CONTINUE TO WORK WITH BWI TO
  DETERMINE/RESOLVE THE CLERICAL ERROR AND DELEGATE THE
  APPROVAL OF THE PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACT WITH BWI TO THE CITY
  MANAGER OR RETURN TO CITY COUNCIL WITH OTHER OPTIONS.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Schmitz, Stegura

B.  MASTER PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT (MPSA) WITH RISK
  MANAGEMENT PROFESSIONALS INCORPORATED FOR THE DEVELOPMENT
  OF AN EMERGENCY OPERATIONS PLAN

  Recommendation: That the City Council Approve a 1) Master Professional Services
  Agreement (MPSA) approved as to form by the City Attorney with Risk Management
  Professionals Incorporated, and 2) Task Order 1-2024, under the MPSA in the not-
  to-exceed amount of $25,000.

Assistant to the City Manager Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPROVE A 1) MASTER PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT (MPSA)
  APPROVED AS TO FORM BY THE CITY ATTORNEY WITH RISK
  MANAGEMENT PROFESSIONALS INCORPORATED, AND 2) TASK ORDER
  1-2024, UNDER THE MPSA IN THE NOT-TO-EXCEED AMOUNT OF $25,000.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Schmitz, Stegura

C.  LETTER OF OPPOSITION TO AB 3093 (WARD) LAND USE: HOUSING ELEMENT:
  STREAMLINED MULTIFAMILY HOUSING

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve and authorize the Mayor to sign the
  letter of opposition.

Assistant to the City Manager Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN stated that the League of California Cities opposed this
bill as well.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JULY 9, 2024
   COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE AND AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR TO SIGN THE LETTER OF
  OPPOSITION.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Schmitz, Stegura

D.  MASTER PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT AND ANNUAL AUDIT
  ENGAGEMENT LETTER TASK ORDER

  Recommendation: That the City of Rolling Hills Estates approve the master
  professional services agreement as approved to form by the City Attorney and Task
  Order No. 2024-01 for the firm of Rogers, Anderson, Malody & Scott, LLP to perform
  the annual audit and report for Fiscal Year 2023-24; perform the single audit, if
  needed; prepare the Pepper Tree Foundation’s tax returns; and review the GANN
  appropriation limitation for a total amount not to exceed $51,405.

Senior Accountant Estrada provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE MASTER PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT AS
  APPROVED TO FORM BY THE CITY ATTORNEY AND TASK ORDER NO.
  2024-01 FOR THE FIRM OF ROGERS, ANDERSON, MALODY & SCOTT, LLP
  TO PERFORM THE ANNUAL AUDIT AND REPORT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2023-
  24; PERFORM THE SINGLE AUDIT, IF NEEDED; PREPARE THE PEPPER
  TREE FOUNDATION’S TAX RETURNS; AND REVIEW THE GANN
  APPROPRIATION LIMITATION FOR A TOTAL AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED
  $51,405.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Schmitz, Stegura

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  QUARTERLY 2023-2024 WORK PLAN UPDATE AND WORK PLAN 2024-2025

  Recommendation: Receive and file.

City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF applauded staff for their hard work on the work plan all year long.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN so ordered.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JULY 9, 2024
 11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF attended the South Bay Cities Council of Governments
(SBCCOG) Steering Committee meeting yesterday.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

None.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

None.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 7:24 p.m. COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN adjourned the meeting Tuesday, August 13,
2024 at 7:00 p.m. for the purpose of a Regular meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit, City Clerk  Frank Zerunyan, Council Member

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
JULY 9, 2024
